SEBoK Information Management, Distilled

Fifth-batch SEBoK distillation, batch 1 of 5 (SE-164). Second SE-internal distillation of Information Management (prior pass at SE-062 plus the SE-039 §VII.6 anchor-reassignment of Cluster F longitudinal-pulverization from CM/SE-097 to IM/SE-114). The fifth-sweep revisit reads the article against §VII.7's matured taxonomy with focus on the longitudinal-pulverization IM-anchor stress-test. The IM page supplies six explicit sub-activities (Collect, Organize, Analyze, Distribute, Protect, Manage End-of-Life) which form a universal-sibling lattice at the IM-engagement rung with ordinal axis (collect precedes organize precedes analyze, etc., per Cluster A sub-form D.5). The five-step information-security framework is a second co-located lattice. The IM-vs-CM relationship — "closely interconnected" with IM ensuring traceability and CM addressing significance relative to specific system elements — confirms IM as the more general substrate-preservation discipline (anchor-reassignment from §VII.6 holds; CM is a sub-instance). Cluster F longitudinal-pulverization at IM-anchor confirmed via three sub-rungs per §VII.7 (CM/version-history, TRA/criterion-conformance trace, DE/integrated-state). The IM page's six-step process pin-art across the engagement plus the data-vs-information distinction supply additional Cluster I and Cluster H readings. Seven clusters compose; longitudinal-pulverization IM anchor revisited and reaffirmed.

II. Source Read

Information Management "plans, executes, and controls the provision of information to designated stakeholders" ensuring it remains unambiguous, complete, verifiable, consistent, traceable, and presentable. ISO/IEC/IEEE 15288 frames IM's purpose as generating, obtaining, confirming, transforming, retaining, retrieving, disseminating, and disposing of information to designated parties. Six sub-activities: Collect (obtain from valid sources, store), Organize (identify, categorize, structure relationships), Analyze (transform and report for decision-making), Distribute (disseminate to authorized stakeholders), Protect (integrity, security, privacy), Manage End-of-Life (obsolescence, archival, disposal). Data-vs-information distinction: "data are raw unstructured values, and information is structured data in context that has been analyzed and interpreted." IM and CM are "closely interconnected"; IM ensures traceability while CM addresses significance relative to specific system elements. Five-step information-security framework: define sensitivity levels, establish classification rules, determine controls, implement controls, monitor compliance. Pitfalls (absent data dictionaries, undefined identification, missing metadata) and good practices (information as strategic asset, planning storage growth, data modeling investment, lifecycle governance).

III. Structural Read

Cluster F (pulverization, Doc 445), longitudinal-pulverization IM-anchor stress-test, reaffirmed. SE-039 §VII.6 reassigned the Cluster F longitudinal-pulverization anchor from CM (SE-047 / SE-097) to IM (SE-062 / SE-114) on the grounds that IM is structurally the more general substrate-preservation discipline. SE-039 §VII.7 reported the IM anchor validated at three sub-rungs (CM version-history, TRA criterion-conformance trace, DE integrated-state). SE-164 stress-tests this anchor reassignment by reading IM directly. The IM page's "Manage End-of-Life" sub-activity, the "lifecycle governance" framing, and the explicit IM-vs-CM relationship ("IM ensures traceability while CM addresses significance relative to specific system elements") all confirm IM as the substrate-preservation general; CM is the specialization to identified configuration-information. The longitudinal-pulverization-IM-anchor reassignment holds. SE-164 is the second instance of IM as the longitudinal-pulverization anchor (after SE-062); the anchor is now load-bearing across two SE-internal readings plus three sub-rungs.

Cluster A (universal-sibling lattice, Doc 572 Appendix D), two co-located lattices. First lattice: the six IM sub-activities (Collect, Organize, Analyze, Distribute, Protect, Manage End-of-Life) are universal-sibling at the IM-engagement rung with ordinal-axis (D.5 sub-form per SE-039 §VII.7). Each activity binds every IM engagement aspect-wise; the discriminator is engagement-aspect; the ordinal partial order is empirical (collect precedes organize precedes analyze; protect and manage-end-of-life are continuous-throughout). Second lattice: the five-step information-security framework (define / establish / determine / implement / monitor) is universal-sibling at the security-engagement rung also with ordinal-axis. Two co-located ordinal-axis lattices: D.5 sub-form gains a fifth load-bearing instance.

Cluster J (engineered-system context, Doc 530), substrate-preservation rung. IM is the general substrate-preservation rung the engagement requires. The "treat information as a strategic asset" framing names the substrate as load-bearing across the engagement's lifetime. Cluster J gains a substrate-preservation-rung instance.

Cluster I (pin-art / temporal-concurrency, Doc 572 Appendix C). IM activities are pin-set across every life-cycle stage; the "lifecycle governance" framing is verbatim Cluster I reading. Complements SE-038 HSI pin-art and SE-160 verification pin-art.

Cluster B (multi-keeper composition, Doc 604), IM-CM keeper coordination. "IM and CM are closely interconnected" is structurally Cluster B coordination-by-rung composition: IM-keeper holds general substrate-preservation; CM-keeper holds configuration-significance; both compose at the substrate-preservation engagement. Cluster B gains a substrate-preservation-rung instance.

Cluster H (hypostatic boundary, Doc 372), data-vs-information distinction. "Data are raw unstructured values; information is structured data in context that has been analyzed and interpreted." This distinction is procedural and operational; the discipline does not claim what data IS at deeper rungs. Worth noting: the data-vs-information distinction itself is structurally analogous to the rung-1-vs-rung-2 substrate-keeper distinction; IM operationalizes the rung distinction at the artifact rung.

Cluster K (virtue constraints, Doc 314), V3-as-procedure-binding at the security and end-of-life sub-activities. The five-step information-security procedure exists because security-by-discretion exhibits rankism (privileged users override controls). The Manage End-of-Life sub-activity exists because retention-by-discretion exhibits complacency (unrepresented retention costs and obsolescence risks). Both sub-activities are V3-as-procedure-binding. Cluster K density grows.

Cluster E (institutional ground, Doc 571), ISO/IEC/IEEE 15288 carrier. IM's purpose is framed by ISO/IEC/IEEE 15288. The standards-body carrier is the institutional ground; the article is single-carrier-anchored at the ISO standard. Standard Cluster E reading.
